title: Yosi Maoni
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 2:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.2.6.13), it is told that he once preached in the synagogue at Tiberias. (In [Bereshit Rabbah 80:1 (Hyman cites the beginning of 81)](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.80.1), he preached in the synagogue of Maon; Hyman treats the accounts as referring to the same place, since Maon was near Tiberias, as explained in Sotah 1:8.) “Hear, O priests”—why do you not toil in Torah? [Etc.] “Did I not give you twenty-four gifts?” They answered, “They give us nothing.” “The king takes everything”—“for yours is the judgment”: “I said this to you.” He meant the house of the patriarchs. Rabbi Yudan the Nasi (the second) heard and became angry; Yosi was afraid and fled. Rabbi Yochanan and Resh Lakish went up to appease the Nasi, saying that Yosi was a great man. He asked, “Can he answer everything I ask him?” They said yes. He asked Yosi what “for their mother has played the harlot” meant: “Was our mother Sarah a harlot?” Yosi replied, “Like daughter, like mother; like mother, like daughter; like the generation, like the Nasi; like the Nasi, like the generation.” This Yerushalmi is cited in [Rabbenu Chananel’s commentary on Sanhedrin 22a](https://www.sefaria.org/Rabbeinu_Chananel_on_Sanhedrin.22a.4), where the name is Rabbi Yosef Maoni. Hyman says the author of Mavo HaYerushalmi erred on this point.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The named Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin2:6 paragraph supports the preaching and dialogue. Hyman’s Bereshit Rabbah chapter81 locator is retained; the older supplied digital parallel was numbered80:1.

The linked Yerushalmi gives Yosi Maoni and the sermon in Tiberias. The linked Midrash describes Yosi Meona’ah in the synagogue of Maon. Rabbenu Chananel’s wording has Rav Yosef Maoni, and [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1933&lang=en) heads his entry “Yosef Meona’ah.” Hyman explains the place names and identifies the patriarch as Yudan II.
